design_decisions.boolean_rc: Add rc0=added/rc1=present-SILENT; Remove rc0=removed/rc1=absent-SILENT — FPC set Booleans, NOT errors (loud contrast with TDictionary's raise-on-dup Add and always-rc0 Remove; README comparison box because the units will be used side by side).
design_decisions.set_algebra: FPC loop semantics cloned: UnionWith = Add each of other's snapshot; IntersectWith = TWO-PASS :2861 (collect victims, then remove — self-intersect is a defined no-op); ExceptWith = Remove each of other's snapshot; SymmetricExceptWith pinned at P0 (self-case must yield empty set). Operand validated as a live THashSet BEFORE any mutation (atomicity — the Assign lesson). Event order on algebra ops = hash iteration order, UNSPECIFIED (tests set-compare).
design_decisions.events: Single onNotify property + public virtual Notify seam + _notifyHook guard (house pattern; unhooked cost = one [[ -n ]]). No TObject* set subclass exists in FPC — seam is future-proofing, documented.
design_decisions.extract_ambiguity: Extract miss -> RESULT='' rc 0 (Default(T), :3019) — identical shape to extracting a stored '' element; disambiguate via Contains first (same pinned ambiguity as tdictionary ExtractPair).

fpc_refs.line_number_note: The :2815/:2853/:2861/:2878/:2886 and :3002/:3009/:3019/:3031 refs recorded at P0 came from a DIFFERENT revision of the same file. The code is identical word for word; only the line numbers moved. Everything below is the tag, and the unit header / README / PLAN were re-pointed to it in this phase.
fpc_refs.AddRange :2379: function TCustomSet<T>.AddRange(constref AValues: array of T): Boolean; begin Result := True; for i in AValues do Result := Add(i) and Result; end;  — AND-fold; Add runs for EVERY item (no short-circuit, the `and` is on the right of the assignment); an empty array leaves Result True, hence zero args = rc 0.
fpc_refs.AddRange TEnumerable overload :2397: same AND-fold with a whole collection as the source — the shape the fpcunit seed uses at :117/:146; our surface is varargs, so that call maps to AddRange over the source's ToArray output (Boolean) plus UnionWith (membership).
fpc_refs.UnionWith :2417: procedure TCustomSet<T>.UnionWith(AHashSet: TCustomSet<T>); begin for i in AHashSet.Ptr^ do Add(i^); end;
fpc_refs.IntersectWith :2425: LList := TList<PT>.Create; for i in Ptr^ do if not AHashSet.Contains(i^) then LList.Add(i); for i in LList do Remove(i^); LList.Free;  — TWO-PASS over SELF, so a.IntersectWith a collects nothing and is a defined no-op.
fpc_refs.ExceptWith :2442: procedure TCustomSet<T>.ExceptWith(AHashSet: TCustomSet<T>); begin for i in AHashSet.Ptr^ do Remove(i^); end;  — a.ExceptWith a walks the argument's (== self's) table while removing; the bash port snapshots first, so the drain is defined: the set ends empty.
fpc_refs.SymmetricExceptWith :2450: LList := TList<PT>.Create; for i in AHashSet.Ptr^ do if Contains(i^) then LList.Add(i) else Add(i^); for i in LList do Remove(i^); LList.Free;  — TWO-PASS over the OPERAND; a.SymmetricExceptWith a marks everything and ends empty (S3 confirmed).
fpc_refs.THashSet Booleans: Add :2559 (`Result := not FInternalDictionary.ContainsKey(AValue); if Result then FInternalDictionary.Add(...)`), Remove :2566, Contains :2593 — the abstract trio TCustomSet (declared :474-527, Add abstract at :505) is written against, which is why the bash ops drive $this.Add/$this.Remove/$this.Contains rather than the storage.
fpc_refs.seed: packages/rtl-generics/tests/tests.generics.sets.pas Test_Set_General :86-152 — hand-computed truth table, ported case for case in section A of tests/005_SetAlgebra.sh: A={0,2,4,6,8} B={1,3,5,7,9} (:96-103); C:=copy(A), C.UnionWith(B)={0..9}, Add(5)=False, AddRange([6,7])=False, Count=10 (:106-111); C.ExceptWith(B)={0,2,4,6,8}, AddRange(B)=True (:114-118); {0..5} XOR {3..9} = {0,1,2,6,7,8,9} (:121-135); {0..5} AND {3..9} = {3,4,5} (:138-148).

deviations: The six members drive the public $this.Add / $this.Remove / $this.Contains instead of inlining the storage idioms. This is FPC's own structure (TCustomSet's procedures call the abstract Add/Remove) and it makes the P3 event stream identical to the same calls made by hand; it costs one member dispatch per element (40 ms per 1000 internal $this.Add vs 27 ms inlined, in a shell where 1000 external Add calls cost 217 ms), well inside the 3x relative gate.

AddRangeFromArray reuses kk._outName (via TSet._outName) for its INPUT name, following tinifile TMemIniFile.SetStrings (tinifile.sh:1263). kk._outName was written for OUTPUT names, but it refuses nothing a legitimate input array could be named: identifier shape, the framework reserved set, the unit's __ts_ prefix and the instance's own _data/_class/_items. No kkore change was needed or made.

A non-array or unset input name is rc 2 as well (new helper TSet._isIndexed, the P9-F3 `local -; set +u` shape around ${ref@a}), so h.AddRangeFromArray no_such_var neither aborts a set -u caller nor silently adds nothing with rc 0.
tests/001_Skeleton.sh's sentinel case was rewritten (not weakened): it now asserts that UnionWith answers rc 1 on a non-set operand and leaves NO sentinel, while Notify still returns one.

The 9 that passed red are the ones a stub cannot break: Remove-miss silence, Clear-on-empty silence, the hook-LESS delete, the empty/rejected-operand silence, survival of a failing callback under `set -eu` in a child bash, the detach case, Extract's RESULT surviving a clobbering callback, the a-UNION-a / a-INTERSECT-a no-ops, and the cost measurement (whose limit is relative to its own baseline).

fpc_refs.TCollectionNotification :112: (cnAdded, cnRemoved, cnExtracted) — the three action tokens, ported verbatim as added/removed/extracted.
fpc_refs.TCustomSet.OnNotify :526: property OnNotify: TCollectionNotifyEvent<T> read GetOnNotify write SetOnNotify; — over the ABSTRACT pair GetOnNotify :495 / SetOnNotify :496. A set has NO virtual Notify in FPC at all; the public virtual `Notify` seam here is the house pattern (tqueuestack/tdictionary), which PLAN 2.4 had already chosen and which P3 amended with what FPC really does.
fpc_refs.THashSet.SetOnNotify :2530: FOnNotify := AValue; if Assigned(AValue) then FInternalDictionary.OnKeyNotify := InternalDictionaryNotify else FInternalDictionary.OnKeyNotify := nil; — with no callback assigned the internal dictionary is NOT HOOKED, i.e. nothing is dispatched. This is the FPC original of the TSet._notify gate: the gate is parity, not an optimisation.
fpc_refs.THashSet.InternalDictionaryNotify :2500: FOnNotify(Self, AItem, AAction); — the SENDER handed to the callback is the SET (Self), not the internal dictionary. Ported as "$on_notify" "$__inst__" "$item" "$action".
fpc_refs.THashSet.GetOnNotify :2525: Result := FInternalDictionary.OnKeyNotify; — reads back the private FORWARDER, not the handler the caller assigned. NOT ported (deviation): $(s.on_notify) returns what was set.
fpc_refs.THashSet.Destroy :2554: FInternalDictionary.Free; — freeing the dictionary runs its Clear, so `removed` fires per element during delete (S5). `$this.Clear` now runs before TSet._teardown.
fpc_refs.THashSet.Add :2559 / Remove :2566 / Extr: the cnAdded / DoRemove(cnRemoved) / DoRemove(cnExtracted) / dictionary-Clear sources of the stream. Extract's miss exits at :2582 BEFORE DoRemove, hence silent (S6).
fpc_refs.seed: packages/rtl-generics/tests/tests.generics.sets.pas Test_TCustomSet_Notification :261-338, entered from Test_THashSet_Notification :340 — ported case for case in section A of tests/006_Events.sh (9 cases). Its LSet deliberately carries NO listener, which also pins that events belong to the RECEIVER and not to the operand; its two EnumerableStrings* AddRange overloads (:277/:278) map to our varargs AddRange as at P2; its final block :330-336 (Add('Polandball') then ASet.Free -> cnAdded then cnRemoved) is the S5 proof.

sequences_pinned.Add: new -> exactly one `added` AFTER the write; duplicate -> NO event and no mutation (S1).
sequences_pinned.Remove: hit -> one `removed` fired AFTER the unset — the callback's Contains is false and Count is already decremented; miss -> nothing (S2).
sequences_pinned.Extract: hit -> one `extracted` after the removal, with kk._return running AFTER the event so a callback that clobbers RESULT cannot corrupt the answer; miss -> nothing, rc 0, RESULT='' (S6).
sequences_pinned.Clear: the storage is emptied FIRST — every callback observes Count 0 — then exactly one `removed` per old element (multiset compare); Clear on an empty set fires nothing (S4).
sequences_pinned.delete: one `removed` per element and then the storage is freed; a hook-less delete fires nothing and still frees (S5).
sequences_pinned.Assign: every `removed` (the old contents) strictly BEFORE every `added` (the new) — asserted by index position, not by shape.
sequences_pinned.AddRange/AddRangeFromArray: `added` for the genuinely new only, in argument order (exact compare).
sequences_pinned.UnionWith/IntersectWith/ExceptWith: `added` for the operand-only elements / `removed` for the victims / `removed` for the hits — multiset-compared against the P2 truth table A={a,b,c,d} B={c,d,e,f}.
sequences_pinned.SymmetricExceptWith: `added` for operand-only (pass 1) ALL before `removed` for the common ones (pass 2); the phase order is deterministic even though the within-phase order is hash order, and the FPC seed :303-304 expects the same.
sequences_pinned.self_ops: a UNION a and a INTERSECT a fire NOTHING; a EXCEPT a and a SYMEXCEPT a fire `removed` x |a| and leave the set empty.
sequences_pinned.no_events: an empty operand fires nothing, and a rejected operand (rc 1 before any mutation) fires nothing.
sequences_pinned.signature: cb <inst> <item> <action>, byte-exact over 12 exotic elements ('' ] [ a]b newline $(touch canary) * it's a\b k kk café) through AddRange and Clear, plus the ''/k/kk trio through Remove/Extract, with a canary proving nothing is executed.

tasks.reentrancy_rule: Callbacks run AFTER the mutation and every loop walks a SNAPSHOT, so a callback that mutates the set sees a CONSISTENT set and its own mutations are delivered as further events (re-entrant). Asserted with the full invariant Count == raw storage subscript count == ToArray count, not with Count alone. Cases: add-during-Clear (3 removed + 1 added, set = {REBORN}), remove-during-UnionWith (c:added d:added a:removed, set = {b,c,d}), Clear-during-Add (zz:added zz:removed, set empty), and a 5-deep bounded recursion (5 `added`, 5 elements). Terminating the recursion is the callback's job — documented in README.md.

hookless_cost.gate: one `[[ -n "$on_notify" || -n "$_notifyHook" ]]` per mutation and NO dispatch
hookless_cost.ratio: 2.6x on both bashes for one virtual dispatch plus a do-nothing callback per element; the test's gate is 5x
hookless_cost.regression_check: the unhooked figure is indistinguishable from the P2 baseline (219 ms on 5.2.37 / 188 ms on 5.3.9). A paired before/after benchmark of Add/Contains/Remove over 1k, three interleaved rounds against `git show HEAD:thashset/thashset.sh`, left Contains — which never calls the gate — unchanged, so the added `var _notifyHook` costs nothing per member frame and the second string test is below measurement noise.

deviations: The gate carries TWO string tests, not one. The phase brief asked for both `hook-less cost = exactly one string test` and the gate `[[ -n $on_notify || -n $_notifyHook ]]`; those are mutually exclusive and _notifyHook won, as in tdictionary (three tests) and tqueuestack (two). Measured cost of the second test: below noise — see hookless_cost.regression_check.

`TSet._pending` was DELETED, not left dead. Its own comment said `thin sentinels; removed as phases land` and `Notify` was its last caller. tests/001 and both surface sweeps (005 section H, 006 section I) still assert that no public member answers with __ths_pending__.

$(s.on_notify) reads back the callback that was assigned, where FPC's GetOnNotify :2525 returns the private forwarder. FPC's own asymmetry is not worth porting; recorded in the README divergence table.
The public virtual `Notify` seam and `_notifyHook` have no FPC counterpart (a set has no Notify there). Already the plan's decision in PLAN 2.4; P3 amended that section with FPC's real plumbing.
onNotify's rejection is rc 2 (a malformed CALL, kcl/README.md 1.2), matching ToArray/AddRangeFromArray, rather than rc 1. Owner-requested in the phase brief.

execution_log.summary: All six `TSet._pending ... P2` stubs replaced with real bodies; `Notify` is the only sentinel left (P3). AddRange = the FPC AND-fold over varargs (:2379): rc 0 iff every item was newly added, Add called for every item, zero args = rc 0, a duplicate inside the argument list = rc 1, silent either way. AddRangeFromArray = the same fold over a caller INDEXED array, with the input name validated through TSet._outName/kk._outName before the nameref is bound and a new TSet._isIndexed probe refusing an associative array, a scalar and an unset name (rc 2, nothing added, no abort under set -u). UnionWith (:2417) adds each of the operand's elements; IntersectWith (:2425) is the two-pass collect-then-remove; ExceptWith (:2442) removes each of the operand's; SymmetricExceptWith (:2450) is the two-pass mark-or-add-then-remove over the OPERAND. All four snapshot the operand's keys before self is touched and validate the operand by CLASS (TSet._isSet, R5) before ANY mutation, so a rejected operand leaves the storage byte-identical (asserted with declare -p before/after, not just Count) and answers rc 1 + one kk.debug line. Self-op edges confirmed against the source: a UNION a = a, a INTERSECT a = a, a EXCEPT a = empty, a SYMEXCEPT a = empty. The loops drive $this.Add/$this.Remove/$this.Contains, which is FPC's own structure and keeps the P3 event stream identical to the same calls made by hand.

The `if Assigned(AValue) … else nil` in :2530 is the FPC original of the _notify gate (nothing is hooked, hence nothing dispatched, when no callback is assigned).
